snpscaper: explore human genetic variation with 1000 Genomes data

Source: R/snpscaper-package.R
snpscaper-package.Rd

snpscaper is a teaching package. It lets you pick any region of the human genome, fetch the genotypes of 2,504 people from 26 populations sampled by the 1000 Genomes Project, and explore how genetic variation is distributed within and between those populations. Everything happens inside R: there is no need for the command line or for downloading files by hand.

Key ideas, briefly

  • SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism): a position in the genome where people differ by a single DNA letter, for example some carry G and others A. Each person carries two copies of every autosome, so at a SNP they carry 0, 1 or 2 copies of the alternative letter (allele). snpscaper stores genotypes as these counts.

  • VCF (variant call format): the standard text file format for storing genotypes. The 1000 Genomes Project publishes one compressed VCF per chromosome, each tens of gigabytes. snpscaper reads only the small slice you ask for, using an index file that tells it where in the big file a region lives.

  • 1000 Genomes Project: an international project that sequenced the genomes of people from 26 populations, grouped into five continental "super-populations": African (AFR), Admixed American (AMR), East Asian (EAS), European (EUR) and South Asian (SAS). See samples_1kg.

Typical workflow

  1. fetch_region() gets genotypes for a gene or a set of coordinates.

  2. filter_snps() removes rare and poorly genotyped SNPs, and optionally SNPs that are strongly correlated with their neighbours (LD pruning).

  3. keep_pops() narrows the data to the populations you want to compare.

  4. as_pca_table() prepares the data for principal component analysis with the FactoMineR and factoextra packages.
